name: Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension including connective tissue disease, congenital heart disease, chronic thromboembolic disease, and lung diseases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria must be met including elevated mPAP ≥ 25 mmHg, PCWP ≤ 15 mmHg, PVR > 3 Wood units, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Right heart catheterization is essential for definitive diagnosis

common.notes: Often angina-like due to right ventricular ischemia

occasional.notes: Sign of elevated right atrial pressure

rare.notes: Due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
May suggest connective tissue disease overlap

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP indicating right ventricular strain
Normal or mildly elevated liver function tests secondary to congestion
No specific serologic markers for idiopathic form
imaging: Right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation on echocardiogram
Elevated pulmonary artery pressure on Doppler echocardiography
Pulmonary artery enlargement on chest CT
Right heart catheterization confirming elevated mPAP and PVR
genetic: BMPR2 gene mutations found in familial and some idiopathic cases
other: 6-minute walk test showing reduced exercise capacity
Electrocardiogram with right axis deviation and right ventricular hypertrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure > 15 mmHg
Echocardiographic evidence of left heart dysfunction
Presence of valvular or myocardial disease

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure such as peripheral edema and ascites
references: Galiè N, Humbert M, Vachiery JL, et al. 2015 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Heart J. 2016 Jan 1;37(1):67-119.
Simonneau G, Montani D, Celermajer DS, et al. Haemodynamic definitions and updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2019 Jan;53(1):1801913.
McLaughlin VV, Archer SL, Badesch DB, et al. ACCF/AHA 2009 Expert Consensus Document on Pulmonary Hypertension.
